The metabolomics panel reveals a striking enrichment of **Phase II - Conjugation of compounds** (Reactome R-HSA-156580; FDR = 0.0, fold enrichment = 178.9) and its subsidiary pathway **Glutathione conjugation** (R-HSA-156590; FDR = 1.96 × 10⁻⁴, fold enrichment = 450.3). Seven of the eight input metabolites map to biological oxidations broadly (FDR = 0.0), and five map to Phase I functionalization, indicating that the treatment strongly perturbs the xenobiotic-metabolizing apparatus of the cell.

**Key driver metabolites.** L-Cysteine (C00097) is the rate-limiting precursor for glutathione biosynthesis, and membership verification confirms its presence in both Phase II conjugation and the glutathione conjugation module. Benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-oxide (C14853), the ultimate carcinogenic metabolite of benzo[a]pyrene metabolism, is verified in glutathione conjugation — it is a canonical substrate for glutathione S-transferases (GSTs), which detoxify this reactive diol epoxide by conjugating it to glutathione. N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl (C20319) is a hydroxylated aromatic amine that also enters Phase II conjugation, while beta-mercaptoethanol (C00928), a sulfhydryl reducing agent, is detected in the broader biological oxidations set, consistent with thiol-disulfide balance disruption. Methimazole (C07190), a flavin-containing monooxygenase (FMO) substrate, is confirmed in Phase I functionalization, reflecting oxidative activation of the treatment compound.

**Biological significance.** The concurrent elevation of these metabolites suggests that the treatment either induces (or overwhelms) the CYP450/FMO Phase I oxidation system and the Phase II glutathione and sulfhydryl conjugation machinery. Elevated benzo[a]pyrene diol epoxide is particularly concerning, as glutathione conjugation is the primary protective route against its DNA-binding and mutagenic effects; accumulation may indicate saturable GST capacity. Coumarin (C05851) and pyrocatechol (C15571) further participate in oxidative metabolism, reinforcing a picture of widespread induction of xenobiotic biotransformation. The presence of L-cysteine alongside these toxins is consistent with a cellular attempt to up-regulate glutathione synthesis for detoxification.

**Upstream/downstream relationships.** No direct linear KEGG-reaction path connects L-cysteine to the benzo[a]pyrene diol epoxide (path length > 6 hops, unreachable), which is expected because they converge only at the level of shared enzymatic conjugation reactions rather than a sequential metabolic chain. Their co-enrichment in the glutathione conjugation pathway is the operative biological relationship.
